generations.name: First generation

productionStart.quote: The first X5 sports activity vehicle rolled off the production line on September 1, 1999.

productionEnd.quote: Production of the E53 X5 began on 1 September 1999 and ceased on 22 September 2006.

assembly.quote: United States: Greer, South Carolina (Plant Spartanburg)

drivetrains.system: permanent four-wheel drive, 38:62 front:rear split (xDrive from the 2003 facelift)
drivetrains.quote: The four-wheel drive system distributed drive torque to the front and rear wheels at a ratio of 38 : 62 percent.

revealed.quote: In July 2003, the facelifted X5 was presented for the 2004 model year at the IAA 2003 in September

quotes: In July 2003, the facelifted X5 was presented for the 2004 model year at the IAA 2003 in September
Production started at BMW's Spartanburg plant on 26 September.

changes.text: The range was revised in 2003, with upgraded engines, refreshed styling and the introduction of xDrive all-wheel drive.
changes.quote: The entire range was revised in 2003 and, while all engines were upgraded and the car's styling subtly refreshed, the big news was the introduction of xDrive.

changes.text: xDrive could vary the torque split between the axles, sending up to 100% to either axle, instead of the fixed 38:62 split.
changes.quote: Instead of using the previous X5 system which consisted of power being split 38:62 (front:rear) and DSC to brake wheels without losing traction, xDrive could vary power to the front or rear axles in milliseconds, transferring up to 100% of engine power to either axle

changes.text: New headlights with corona rings and enlarged kidney grilles.
changes.quote: The grilles were enlarged, as well as their actual slats being modified in a 'flame surfaced' style. In keeping with the E39 facelift of 2001, the 2004 X5's headlights got corona rings around all four headlamp projectors.

changes.text: The 4.6is was replaced by a 4.8is model in 2004.
changes.quote: In 2004, the 4.6is was replaced by a 4.8is model

changes.text: Adaptive headlights became available, only with xenon headlights.
changes.quote: Adaptive Headlights (available only with xenon HID headlamps

notes: Wikipedia also lists BMW de México (Toluca) as an assembly site, but BMW's 2006 release says the first-generation X5 was 'built exclusively at BMW Manufacturing' in South Carolina; only Spartanburg is recorded.
Wikipedia's infobox gives US model years 2000–2007, which overlaps the E70's 2007 model year; model years are therefore not recorded here.

Engine years in the table are as given by Wikipedia ('Years' column); it is not stated whether they are calendar or model years. The 4.4i was the launch engine; BMW UK says six-cylinder petrol and diesel variants followed in 2001.
No Commons category exists for the facelift.

changes.text: Wheelbase of 2,933 mm, 113 mm longer than the previous X5.
changes.quote: The new BMW X5 has a wheelbase measuring 2,933mm, up 113mm compared to the previous X5

changes.text: 187 mm longer and 17 mm wider (including mirrors) than the previous X5.
changes.quote: Compared to the previous X5 this model is 187mm longer and 17mm wider (including mirrors).

changes.text: First BMW available with an optional third row of seats, for up to seven occupants.
changes.quote: The BMW X5 is the first BMW capable of being specified with a third row of seats. A total of seven occupants can now be transported.

changes.text: First BMW with double-wishbone front suspension.
changes.quote: the car is the first BMW product to come with a double wishbone front suspension

changes.text: iDrive control system fitted to the X5 for the first time.
changes.quote: Inside, a new design of dashboard houses BMW's iDrive control system fitted to the X5 for the first time.

changes.text: The manual gearbox was dropped, leaving only automatic transmissions.
changes.quote: The manual transmission is entirely dropped, leaving only the automatic transmission.

changes.text: First SAV (sports activity vehicle) in the world offered with a head-up display, and the first with run-flat tyres as standard.
changes.quote: It is now the first SAV in the world to be offered with Head-up Display and also the first to come with Run-flat tyres as standard.

revealed.quote: In 2010 the X5 underwent a "Life Cycle Impulse" (LCI) update, debuted at the New York Auto Show in April 2010 and introduced as 2011 models in BMW North America markets.

changes.text: A new range of turbocharged direct-injection engines was introduced.
changes.quote: More significantly, a new range of engines, all turbocharged and with direct injection was introduced.

changes.text: An eight-speed automatic became standard on all versions.
changes.quote: All versions of the new BMW X5 are equipped with an eight-speed automatic transmission as standard.

changes.text: BMW states fuel consumption and emissions up to 10 percent lower than before.
changes.quote: In spite of significantly improved performance, fuel consumption and emission levels are up to 10 percent lower compared to its predecessor.

changes.text: Larger side air intakes at the front and more body-coloured surfaces on the front and rear aprons.
changes.quote: Larger side air intakes at the front and an increased proportion of surfaces painted in body colour within the area of the front and rear end aprons

changes.text: Redesigned L-shaped tail lights with two LED light banks each.
changes.quote: The L-shaped, redesigned taillights, each with two homogeneously illuminated LED light banks

notes: BMW UK gives the wheelbase gain over the E53 as 113 mm; Wikipedia says 110 mm longer wheelbase and 165 mm longer body. The manufacturer figures are recorded.
Wikipedia's infobox gives North American model years 2007–2014, which overlaps the F15's 2014 model year; only the start (2007) is recorded.

The X5 M (E70) was introduced in 2009 for the 2010 model year; Wikipedia says it was introduced at the New York Auto Show in April 2009, while a BMW US pricing release (not read in full) reportedly says the X5 M made its world debut in Shanghai. Not resolved.
UK 'hp' figures in BMW UK releases are metric horsepower (PS); recorded as stated.
Seating (5 standard, optional 7) is described in sources only in words, so it is recorded via changes rather than the seating field.
No Commons category exists for the LCI or as a separate E70 X5 M category beyond 'Category:BMW X5 M (E70)'.

notes: European launch engines carried EU names (xDrive40i 250 kW/340 hp, M50d); the V8 xDrive50i was not sold in Europe, and for the 2020 model year the US got the M50i in its place. US figures are SAE hp (xDrive40i 335 hp).

BMW announced in Feb 2023 that facelift production would begin in April 2023; Wikipedia says the LCI entered production in March 2023. The manufacturer date is recorded. The facelift press kit is dated 8 Feb 2023 and the US debut was at The Amelia in March 2023.

Wikipedia lists production ending in 2026 (succeeded by the G65). Avtotor (Russia) assembled some X5s from leftover kits in 2025 without BMW's involvement (Wikipedia); not recorded as an assembly site.
The iX5 Hydrogen (G05-based fuel-cell demonstration fleet of fewer than 100 vehicles, 2023) is not recorded as a powertrain.
UK release lists xDrive50e as 490hp 'including temporary boost effect'; US release lists 483 hp. Both recorded with their market.
Cargo standard 'EPA' is as printed in the US spec table. No Commons category exists for the facelift.
